name: Exemestane (aromatase inhibitor endocrine therapy)
cyclesNote: continuous once-daily dosing for 5 years (adjuvant), extended to 7.5 to 10 years total may be considered for node-positive disease; continued until progression or unacceptable toxicity in metastatic disease

source.textbook: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.

institution.provenance: ONCQIS grounded Standard Protocol (experimental, owner/device test only; not clinically activated)

biomarkers.note: Endocrine therapy REQUIRES hormone-receptor-positive disease (ER and/or PR positive). Exemestane is a steroidal aromatase inhibitor (aromatase inactivator) and works only in a low-estrogen (postmenopausal) environment: it is used in postmenopausal patients, or in premenopausal patients ONLY with concurrent ovarian function suppression/ablation (exemestane plus ovarian suppression was a SOFT/TEXT arm). HER2 is tested to guide added HER2-directed therapy and does not change the endocrine indication. Per DeVita 12th ed. (Chapter 16) and Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Invasive Breast Cancer, Principles of Adjuvant Endocrine Therapy (BINV-K).

histology: hormone-receptor-positive invasive breast carcinoma (histology-agnostic; includes invasive ductal carcinoma (IDC) and invasive lobular carcinoma (ILC))
supportiveCare: Not myelosuppressive; no G-CSF or routine antiemetics required (oral endocrine therapy).

Ovarian suppression (OFS) is MANDATORY when used in premenopausal patients: GnRH agonist (e.g., goserelin 3.6 mg SC every 4 weeks) or surgical/radiation ablation; exemestane plus OFS was a SOFT/TEXT regimen. Per NCCN v6.2026 BINV-K 2 of 4 and 3 of 4; DeVita lines 185051 to 185084.

Bone health: aromatase inhibitors increase fracture risk and cause bone loss; monitor bone mineral density and consider a bisphosphonate or denosumab plus calcium/vitamin D (NCCN v6.2026 BINV-K footnote q).
Arthralgia/myalgia and steroidal-type effects (weak androgenic properties at higher doses) may occur (DeVita lines 30196 to 30204).
monitoring: adherence to daily oral endocrine therapy (crucial to outcome)
bone mineral density (baseline and periodic) given fracture risk
in premenopausal patients on OFS: confirm ongoing postmenopausal-range estradiol; vaginal bleeding on an AI warrants urgent review
clearanceChecks: postmenopausal status confirmed (or OFS in place for premenopausal)

doseModificationRules.text: Options include switching to another aromatase inhibitor after a washout, or to tamoxifen; supportive measures include exercise, NSAIDs, or duloxetine (NCCN v6.2026 supportive-care discussion; DeVita lines 30196 to 30204). Physician decides.

drugs.name: Exemestane
drugs.notes: Source: DeVita 12th ed. lines 30205 and 30208. Exemestane 25 mg by mouth once daily, continuous (flat daily dosing; the days array marks once-daily administration within a nominal 1-day cycle). Steroidal aromatase inhibitor (irreversible aromatase inactivator). Adjuvant duration 5 years, with extended aromatase inhibitor duration (7.5 to 10 years total) considered for node-positive disease (NCCN v6.2026 BINV-K).

provenance.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.
provenance.locator: lines 30205 and 30208 (FDA-approved dose 25 mg per day; administered once daily by mouth, recommended daily dose 25 mg)
